title: Conditionals — practice quiz
description: A short check on `if` branches, comparisons, `and` / `or` / `not`, and `match`. This quiz does not run GDScript; it only checks that the ideas landed.

questions.prompt: In an `if` / `elif` / `else` chain, when does `else` run?
choices: Every time, after the other branches
Only when every `if` and `elif` above it was false
Only when the flashlight is on
questions.explain: `else` is the fallback. It runs only when none of the `if` or `elif` conditions above it were true.

questions.prompt: What does `and` mean in `mic_volume > threshold and distance_to_player <= hear_distance`?
choices: The check passes if either side is true
The check passes only if both sides are true
The check flips true to false
questions.explain: `and` means both sides must be true. The monster hears you only if you are loud enough and close enough. `or` is the one that passes when either side is true.

questions.prompt: What does `not is_flashlight_on` mean when the flashlight is on?
questions.explain: `not` flips a `bool`. If the flashlight is on, `is_flashlight_on` is `true`, so `not is_flashlight_on` is `false`.

questions.prompt: In a `match`, what is the `_` branch?
choices: The first branch that always runs
The fallback, for any value that did not match an earlier branch
questions.explain: The `_` branch is the safety net, like `else`. It runs when the value did not match any named branch above it.
